title: Sprint Reserve Ledger: predictive skill-burn model & soft-descope algorithm
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Problem: In constrained cycles we repeatedly face last-minute capacity shortfalls across kernel, infra, and frontend teams. Current triage is manual and opaque; feature owners lose predictability. Proposal: build a lightweight 'Sprint Reserve Ledger' workflow + a small predictive skill-burn model that estimates how many story points (by skill tag) the upcoming cycle can absorb, then run a soft-descope scoring algorithm to recommend de-scopes ranked by business value / implementation friction. Deliverables: 1) workshop template for rapid essentialization, 2) a simple predictive spreadsheet + scoring heuristics, 3) a repeatable handoff (PM -> Eng leads) and a rollout/comm protocol for go/no-go decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Workshop template validated in at least two teams and retrospective notes show faster decision time (target < 60m)
Predictive skill-burn model produces a capacity estimate within +/- 15% of actual staffed velocity across a trial of two cycles
Soft-descope algorithm ranks candidate tickets and PM/Eng agree on top-3 de-scopes in >= 75% of trial runs
Runbook created: who owns the ledger, who makes final cut decisions, and where to record official scope changes (Confluence + Linear)
proposal_summary: Run a 90-minute cross-functional workshop mid-planning to stabilize assumptions, collect skill-level availability (backend, infra, frontend, SRE), and produce a ledger of: committed points, predicted burn, and guardrails. Feed ledger into a small rules engine (initially a Google Sheet with formulas) that applies Business Value / Risk / Rework cost heuristics to candidate scope items and outputs a ranked descope list. Automate two small checks: (1) flag tickets with infra dependencies; (2) surface customer-facing regressions for manual review. Iterate on heuristics after two cycles.
success_metrics: Median time to finalize scope during planning reduced from current baseline to <= 60 minutes
Percentage of cycles that hit >90% of planned MVS reduced by 30% (fewer surprise de-scopes mid-cycle)
Stakeholder satisfaction (PM/Eng leads) survey score for planning decisions >= 4/5 after pilot
Number of emergency unplanned de-scopes during cycle reduced by 50% in pilot teams
risks: Model accuracy risk: early predictions may under/overestimate velocity for unfamiliar teams
Behavioral risk: teams may game the ledger (inflating estimates) without clear audit/penalty signals
Tooling risk: a spreadsheet-based approach may create fragmentation if not standardized; needs central template
Decision ownership: fuzzy escalation path could cause last-minute unilateral cuts by engineering without PM alignment
rollout_plan: Week 1: Draft workshop template and ledger sheet; collect feedback from three pilot PMs
Week 2: Run pilot workshop with infra, backend, frontend leads for two initiatives; record decisions and time-to-decision
Week 3: Refine model heuristics and build a tiny automation to pull estimated assigned-headcounts from HR/rota (manual CSV initially)
Week 4: Publish runbook and Confluence template; train on-call PM/EM rotation to own ledger in planning cadence
Post-pilot (Next cycle): Measure metrics, incorporate lessons, and propose light-weight Console integration for the ledger if adoption justifies engineering effort
